question: From ________ onwards, Economic Survey in India has been delinked from the Union Budget.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1964**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Economic Survey in India was delinked from the Union Budget starting from the year **1964**.
 
• The Economic Survey is presented in the Parliament before the Union Budget.
 
• The Economic Survey provides a comprehensive overview of the country's economic development over the past year.
 
• It is an important document that helps in understanding the economic challenges and opportunities facing the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Survey**

 
 
• The Economic Survey is an annual document released by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
 
• It is presented in the Parliament ahead of the Union Budget and is considered an important precursor to the budget.
 
• The Survey reviews the developments in the Indian economy over the past financial year, summarizes the performance on major development programs, and highlights the policy initiatives of the government and the prospects of the economy in the short to medium term.
 
• The document is prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance under the guidance of the Chief Economic Advisor.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget**
 
 
• The Union Budget of India, also referred to as the Annual Financial Statement, is the annual budget of the Republic of India.
 
• The Government presents it on the first day of February so that it can be materialized before the beginning of the new financial year in April.
 
• The budget is divided into revenue budget and capital budget. The revenue budget includes the government's revenue receipts and expenditure, while the capital budget includes the government's capital receipts and payments.
 
• The Budget is a crucial document that lays down the government's financial strategy and priorities for the upcoming financial year.
 
 
 
• **Chief Economic Advisor**
 
 
• The Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) is a position in the Government of India, usually an economist of high repute, who is responsible for advising the government on economic matters.
 
• The CEA heads the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs and is responsible for the preparation of the Economic Survey.
 
• The CEA also provides inputs on various economic policies and strategies, and plays a key role in drafting and formulating economic policies.
 
• The position of the CEA is critical for the formulation of policies that aim to foster economic growth and stability.
